## d1897119-e054-4e2a-a2fd-06958f8ce0bd / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official 6–20 cm reach-and-hold distribution. Experiment 1 established that the PPO recipe learns the task, but its best measured checkpoint reached only 51.0% on the protected 200-episode development panel. The training proxy peaked near 0.95 while protected-task success remained near one half, so the proxy does not identify an acceptable policy. The 100352-step checkpoint is the current working and best-known candidate because it has the highest measured protected-task success, not because its one-episode margin is robust.

**Lessons and limits:** The baseline sampled training targets only from 14–20 cm, while the protected panel covers 6–20 cm. On that panel, the working checkpoint succeeded on 3/57 (5.3%) targets at 6–10 cm, 32/59 (54.2%) at 10–15 cm, and 67/84 (79.8%) at 15–20 cm; angle sectors were comparatively balanced. The raw log shows learnability and late proxy saturation, but does not establish why short-radius behavior is weak. The three measured checkpoints differ by at most seven episodes overall and were all measured on the same development panel, so checkpoint ranking and intervention effects remain uncertain. The task-reference panel is not the official final assessment.

**Open questions:** It is unresolved whether the training-distribution mismatch is a material cause of short-radius failures, whether the existing representation transfers across the full radius range, and whether improved short-radius behavior can coexist with the established long-radius behavior. The amount of checkpoint-to-checkpoint and panel-to-panel variation also remains unknown.

## d1897119-e054-4e2a-a2fd-06958f8ce0bd / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official 6–20 cm reach-and-hold distribution. Experiment 1 established that the PPO recipe learns the task, but its best measured checkpoint reached only 51.0% on the protected 200-episode development panel and the training proxy did not identify an acceptable policy. Experiment 2 changed only the training target-radius support to the full official range and, after transfer from the experiment-1 working policy, produced a best measured checkpoint at 82.5% (165/200). This is substantial progress toward the objective, but it remains development evidence from one fixed panel rather than official confirmation.

**Lessons and limits:** The baseline sampled training targets only from 14–20 cm, while the protected panel covers 6–20 cm. The experiment-2 working checkpoint improved the radius bands from 3/57 to 50/57 at 6–10 cm and from 32/59 to 54/59 at 10–15 cm, but changed 15–20 cm from 67/84 to 61/84. The experiment-2 endpoint reached 51/57 in the short band but only 80.5% overall, so late training is non-monotonic and the short-radius gain can trade against long-radius behavior. Transfer from the parent and the absence of a contemporaneous unchanged control mean the radius intervention is associated with the gain but is not isolated as its cause. Training proxies reached 1.00 during experiment 2 while protected success remained below the objective, so they remain non-acceptance signals. All six development measurements used the same task-reference-v1 panel and seed 7300; checkpoint ranking, panel variation, and reproducibility therefore remain uncertain. The task-reference panel is not the official final assessment.

**Open questions:** It is unresolved whether additional optimization of the full-radius recipe from the 200704-step working checkpoint can improve beyond 82.5%, has plateaued, or is degrading; whether short-radius improvement can coexist with stable 15–20 cm behavior; and how robust the observed gain is to learning-process and panel variation. The experiment-2 result also does not by itself separate the contribution of radius coverage from transfer and other recipe history.

scientific_question: Can emphasizing the hardest short-radius training band recover the current policy's short- and mid-radius failures without sacrificing its recovered long-radius behavior on the official 6-20 cm distribution?
scientific_strategy:
## d1897119-e054-4e2a-a2fd-06958f8ce0bd / Scientific strategy

**Current synthesis:** The campaign objective is at least 98% success on the official 6–20 cm reach-and-hold distribution. Experiment 1 established that the PPO recipe learns the task, but its best measured checkpoint reached only 51.0% on the protected 200-episode development panel. Experiment 2 expanded training target-radius support to the full official range and produced 82.5% (165/200) after transfer. Experiment 3 continued that unchanged recipe; its endpoint reached 83.0% on the repeated task-reference panel and 87.5% on a fresh 400-episode research panel. The campaign has therefore demonstrated substantial but insufficient development progress, with no official confirmation.

**Lessons and limits:** The baseline sampled training targets only from 14–20 cm, while the protected panel covers 6–20 cm. Experiment 2 improved the working checkpoint to 50/57 at 6–10 cm and 54/59 at 10–15 cm, but reduced 15–20 cm to 61/84. In experiment 3, the unchanged continuation's task-reference sequence was 78.0%, 80.5%, and 83.0%; the endpoint changed the bands relative to the experiment-2 parent to 42/57, 50/59, and 74/84. Thus late optimization recovered long-radius behavior while giving back short- and mid-radius successes. On the fresh research panel, the endpoint had 46 endpoint-only successes versus 30 parent-only successes, but this is a development comparison under that evaluator, not an official result. Training proxies reached 1.00 while task success remained below the objective, so they remain non-acceptance signals. The repeated task-reference measurements use one fixed panel and seed 7300, and the fresh comparison uses one seed 9100; panel and learning-process variation remain uncertain. The target-sampling intervention in experiment 4 changes exposure, not the official evaluator, task mechanics, observation layout, action mapping, or policy I/O.

**Open questions:** It remains unresolved whether emphasizing the hardest short-radius band during training can recover its failures while preserving long-radius behavior, and how robust the current ranking is across panels and training seeds. The contribution of radius coverage, transfer, and later optimization is not isolated by these experiments.
